purpose: The D3 comparison's sequential arm, and the shakedown run that found three defects the fan-out's own instrument made visible.

dial.source: run-args.json — the first run in this project's history to record its own launch configuration

outcome: shipped, verdict PASS, no gate paused under --unattended
why_three_launches: launch 1 was killed by claude -p's 600s background-task ceiling, mid-WIRE — the finding that CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=0 is required for the headless lane
launch 2 died on an API transport error (expired SSL certificate)
launch 3 resumed from MAP SCOPES and ran to ship in one go
defects_this_run_found: a build leg can skip its `reduce ingest` step, report green, and be accepted by the round — the confirm stage re-verifies the T0 artifact and nothing else. env-parsing's task stayed `pending` with 0 ACs ticked while its code was written and T0 was green. Visible only because the leg-completion ledger had a row for schema-rules and none for env-parsing.

an out-of-band ingest inflates a leg's recorded interval and can manufacture concurrency: repairing env-parsing by hand 250.8s late made this dial-1 run report `max_concurrent: 2 (exact)`. The instrument now measures the legs' own T0 windows as well and answers `disputed` instead.

EVAL cited `node --test` where the acceptance contract's literal grading command is `npm test`. The specified command fails on this Node version and the equivalent-looking one passes, so the discrepancy shipped with a PASS.
not_usable_for_d3: env-parsing's leg has no honest end — its ingest never ran inside the leg, and the repair timestamp is the operator's, not the leg's. The D3 comparison is measured on a later pair of runs taken on the fixed harness.
